entries.speaker: Orso Hawker
entries.title: Orso Hawker: ""Good morning, Mr. President.""
entries.dialogueText: "Good morning, Mr. President."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "They placed the draft for the Emerg..."
entries.dialogueText: They placed the draft for the Emergency act in front of me.

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: ""It's because Mr. Ricter made it kn..."
entries.dialogueText: "It's because Mr. Ricter made it known that our administration is blocking the reforms. Many are protesting against that now too."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Not long after, Orso and Lucian arr..."
entries.dialogueText: Not long after, Orso and Lucian arrived.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Greetings.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Greetings.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Finally, you're here.""
entries.dialogueText: “Finally, you're here."

entries.speaker: Livia Suno
entries.title: Livia Suno: ""Understood, sir. I'll take your co..."
entries.dialogueText: "Understood, sir. I'll take your coat now."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I was walking to my office. Today w..."
entries.dialogueText: I was walking to my office. Today was the day to finally write the Emergency Act and order the execution of the decree.

entries.speaker: Livia Suno
entries.title: Livia Suno: ""Fine, thank you.""
entries.dialogueText: "Fine, thank you."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Talks with the leading figures of t..."
entries.dialogueText: Talks with the leading figures of the Old Guards were fruitful and the preparation for the emergency was already underway.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I feel better now that I've seen y..."
entries.dialogueText: “I feel better now that I've seen you, Livia."
entries.menuText: “I feel better now that I've seen you, Livia."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Livia left to hang up my coat. I wa..."
entries.dialogueText: Livia left to hang up my coat. I walked into my office and sat down.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I walked in the marble corridors of..."
entries.dialogueText: I walked in the marble corridors of the Palace, thinking about the huge decisions I was going to make.

entries.speaker: Livia Suno
entries.title: Livia Suno: ""I'm sorry to hear that.""
entries.dialogueText: "I'm sorry to hear that."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "My secretary greeted me at the entr..."
entries.dialogueText: My secretary greeted me at the entrance to my presidential office.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Good morning everybody.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Good morning everybody.”

entries.speaker: Livia Suno
entries.title: Livia Suno: ""Good morning, Mr. President.""
entries.dialogueText: "Good morning, Mr. President."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I'm just fine.""
entries.dialogueText: “I'm just fine."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I'm about to make stressful decisi..."
entries.dialogueText: “I'm about to make stressful decisions. So, not feeling that great.”
entries.menuText: “I'm about to make stressful decisions. So, not feeling that great.”

entries.speaker: Livia Suno
entries.title: Livia Suno: ""Thank you, Mr. President.""
entries.dialogueText: "Thank you, Mr. President."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""How are you today?""
entries.dialogueText: "How are you today?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Good morning, Livia.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Good morning, Livia.”

entries.speaker: Livia Suno
entries.title: Livia Suno: ""Whatever you say, sir. I'll take y..."
entries.dialogueText: "Whatever you say, sir. I'll take your coat now."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""You're right, sweetheart. It isn't..."
entries.dialogueText: "You're right, sweetheart. It isn't your place."
entries.menuText: "You're right, sweetheart. It isn't your place."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""You may be right. But I just don't..."
entries.dialogueText: "You may be right. But I just don't see any other way out of this."
entries.menuText: "You may be right. But I just don't see any other way out of this."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I'm your boss, Livia. Don't questi..."
entries.dialogueText: “I'm your boss, Livia. Don't question my decisions."
entries.menuText: “I'm your boss, Livia. Don't question my decisions."

entries.speaker: Livia Suno
entries.title: Livia Suno: ""That's good to hear.""
entries.dialogueText: "That's good to hear."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "She averted her eyes away from me a..."
entries.dialogueText: She averted her eyes away from me and smiled.

entries.speaker: Livia Suno
entries.title: Livia Suno: ""More importantly, how are you, sir?""
entries.dialogueText: "More importantly, how are you, sir?"

entries.speaker: Livia Suno
entries.title: Livia Suno: ""How are you today, sir?""
entries.dialogueText: "How are you today, sir?"

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "After carefully examining the draft..."
entries.dialogueText: After carefully examining the draft and my own notes, I buried myself in the papers.

entries.speaker: Orso Hawker
entries.title: Orso Hawker: ""It's time to start the emergency p..."
entries.dialogueText: "It's time to start the emergency period. The situation on the streets got worse after we last met."

entries.speaker: Orso Hawker
entries.title: Orso Hawker: ""Regardless of who they are or what..."
entries.dialogueText: "Regardless of who they are or what they support, the situation is clear. Let's see how we'll proceed with the President's decree."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "She paused before taking my coat. I..."
entries.dialogueText: She paused before taking my coat. It looked like she had something on her mind.

entries.speaker: Livia Suno
entries.title: Livia Suno: ""Mr. Rayne, it may not be my place..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. Rayne, it may not be my place to say this, but I'm wondering about your reasoning behind this emergency act. The people want reforms, and delaying them will only lead to more violence."
